correctness.rationale: Separate bounds imply F([0,1]) subset [0,1]. For any positive fixed r, delta=(1-r)G(r) and 1-delta-P(r)=1-G(r)>=0; monotonic P yields the exact no-crossing inequality on both sides. Between consecutive fixed roots, the sign of F(x)-x is constant; barrier invariance forces each orbit monotone and bounded, whence it converges to an endpoint fixed point. All endpoints, degeneracies and the finite-root property are covered. Exact symbolic checks establish example roots, multipliers and contrast two-cycle. No finite computation is used to infer the all-order statement.

value.rationale: In higher-order SIS contagion, the possibility of several stable endemic outcomes makes complete global basins mathematically and epidemiologically meaningful. The result separates true bistability from discrete-time cycling under the largest separate probability-valid infection and recovery coefficients; it applies even when F is nonmonotone, and the radical bistable example gives an exact intervention-seeding threshold. This is not a one-parameter routine numerical increment.
